conflicts: Brief Alignment proposes: Retain the full title, controls, Start action, HUD, skier, gates, and trees, but reduce or lift the title card so more of the downhill route is visibly traceable behind it. Literal completeness alone can yield a checklist-like screen unless required content is transformed into content-specific visual storytelling. Clarity proposes: Reduce the title panel's height and lift it slightly to reveal more of the slope while preserving the title as the first read. Aggressive simplification and a single predictable focal path can make the result safe, uniform, and forgettable. Visual System & Craft proposes: Choose a base pixel unit and snap all scene geometry, borders, shadows, icons, and decorative marks to multiples of it. Over-standardizing geometry, color, component construction, and effects risks flattening semantically different roles into the same generic treatment.
accept: Accept all requested content, a readable focal structure, and a disciplined shared craft system as constraints. Accept reduced arbitrary effects and consistent secondary components, provided the hero, important states, and meaningfully different content roles retain distinctive visual treatment.
compromise: Preserve the content-motivated expressive action: Integrate the title and start prompt into the game world's pixel HUD, add content-driven slope variety such as tracks, moguls, and one iconic hazard, and give the skier a more distinctive animation pose or trail while preserving the strict pixel language. Build it with Craft's shared tokens, place it within Clarity's dominant/secondary structure, and attach it directly to Brief Alignment's requested roles. Keep supporting UI restrained, but allow the hero and semantically different states purposeful variation in scale, silhouette, texture, or color; reject random decoration and generic uniformity alike.
audit_note: Independent persona-preserving MAD cross-critique using the brief, shared r0 screenshot, own critique, and the other three axis suggestions; no moderator output, revised HTML, FUSED/CEN_MAD material, or scores were inspected.
